steps.text: This video shows how to build a subject flow: the actions that run when an agent, or the AI, completes an activity with a disposition. It covers the Finish, Try Again and New Activity actions, and what the Convert Lead action adds.

chapters.title: Why flows
chapters.subtitle: The disposition decides the next step

steps.text: When a call ends, somebody has to decide what happens next. Try again tomorrow, book a follow-up, or stop calling this person.
A subject flow puts that decision in one place. Each disposition has one or more actions.
So agents only pick the outcome, and the follow-up work is created for them, the same way every time.

Open Interaction Center, Management, Subject Flows, and click Manage Flow next to the subject. A new flow is empty. Click Add Action, and pick the type: Finish, Try Again, New Activity, or Convert Lead, which appears with the CRM.

Finish completes the activity and nothing else happens. Pick the disposition it responds to, here Not Interested. When to choose this disposition is guidance the AI reads when it picks an outcome. It starts as the disposition's own description. Show communication preferences lets the action flag the contact, here Do not call, and with the CRM, set the status of a lead. Click Create.
Try Again creates a new try of the same activity, with the attempt count raised by one. Pick No Answer, and set the maximum attempts, here three tries in total.

The assignment type keeps the same owner, or gives the follow-up to a specific user. Default schedule hours says how many hours later it is scheduled, here 24. The agent can change the date on the Complete page. Click Create.

New Activity creates a new activity, for the same subject or another one. Pick Interested, and the target subject, here Test Drive Follow-up. The new activity takes its campaign, channel and interaction type from that subject.
Set its urgency, and the hours until it is scheduled, here 48. A disposition can have several actions, for example Finish and New Activity together.
Back in the list, the Missing flow badge is gone, because the subject now has actions.

chapters.title: Convert Lead
chapters.subtitle: Turn a qualified lead into a contact

steps.text: With the CRM on, Convert Lead converts a lead when an activity ends with a chosen disposition. It chooses the account, whether to create an opportunity, and what happens to the open activities. It runs before the other actions, so a follow-up lands on the new contact.

chapters.title: What the agent sees
chapters.subtitle: The preview on the Complete page

steps.text: When the agent picks a disposition on the Complete page, a preview lists the actions that will run.
Each follow-up shows a Schedule at date and Preparation notes, which become the instructions of the new activity.
If you change the flow, activities already scheduled keep working, and new completions use the new actions.
Retry unanswered calls a few times, then stop.
Book a follow-up automatically when a customer is interested.
Stop calling people who say they are not interested.
Convert a lead the moment it qualifies.
Give every disposition an action, and the next step happens by itself. The user manual and the technical guide are linked in the description. Thanks for watching.
